turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, Mr. Rao walked in without a token, err, he is quite worked up about his face.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sit, sit. What happened, tell me from the start.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Since today morning only, doctor, the left side of the face is hanging. I cannot close this eye, and whistling is not happening. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): It was there the moment you woke?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm, I woke near six and it was already like that. I don't know the exact minute, doctor.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before that, any pain in the ear or the face?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Left ear was paining yesterday. Today it is only a little bit. Afternoon or night, I cannot say, I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Show me both arms up. Any weakness in the arm or the leg?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Arms are fine, I held the bus rail itself. Leg also normal.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And speech? Words getting mixed, or people not following you?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No, speech is normal only. Smile is crooked and I cannot whistle, that is all. My wife got scared after she laughed.
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Last night the home machine showed one-forty over ninety. I checked 2 times.
[SEG0013] person_1 (NURSE): Right. He told me that outside, one-forty over ninety. Just now I checked. Blood pressure is one thirty six over eighty four, pulse 78, temperature thirty six point eight.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): He also said he skips the BP tablet on Sundays.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No no, sister, not Sunday. Saturday I miss it, market day. Other days I take.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Which tablet, what strength?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodipin, five milligram, one in the morning, for the BP. I am having BP for five-ish years. Which year it started I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): And last month a small cut on the thumb, he said it healed in five days.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, it healed normal only, no problem. I don't know why that matters.
[SEG0020] person_1 (NURSE): Sleep also, he said he is sleeping badly for two nights.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): That is true. Sleep is not coming, I keep thinking.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. Nothing.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok, a few other things. Any fever?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Yesterday evening I felt a little warm, today I don't think so. Maybe nothing. I cannot say.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough, cold, running nose?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight coming down?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): No, same only.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Urine? Burning, or going again and again?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. Urine is fine.

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Let me see. Eyebrows up... left forehead is not moving. Close the eyes... left one stays open, sclera is showing. Smile... left corner is flat. Try to whistle... air leaks out. Both grips are equal, no arm drift.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Err, my first plan was to treat this as a stroke, send you for CT brain and start aspirin seventy five milligram today.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Stroke? I don't know, doctor. Is the face going to stay like this?

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am changing my mind. Forehead is involved and the arm and speech are spared, so this is peripheral, not an upper motor neuron stroke. No CT, no aspirin. Working impression is Bell's palsy, the facial nerve is inflamed, the ear pain yesterday fits. Not a final label, we will watch it.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Then what to do? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): We start prednisolone sixty milligram once a day, by mouth, for five days, then I taper when I see you. For the eye, carboxymethylcellulose drops, one drop in the left eye every two hours while awake, and at night you tape the eye shut so the cornea does not dry.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Sixty milligram is heavy, no? I should buy the drops today itself?
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, start today, take it with food in the morning. Come back in one week either way. If the eye becomes very red or the arm turns weak, come to casualty, do not wait.

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
